TRACE-X Compliance Program
==========================

Generated : 2026-09-17T04:42:11.132698+00:00
By        : supervisor
Readiness : 29.0% over 100 scored controls

SCOPE
  The TRACE-X multi-source investigative analytics application (CDR/IPDR, banking and social media), its Postgres system of record and Neo4j knowledge graph, and the evidence lifecycle from ingest through analysis to certified export.

OUT OF SCOPE
  The deploying agency's corporate estate — email, end-user devices, network perimeter, physical premises and HR processes. Those controls are listed with owner 'agency' so the boundary is auditable, never silently omitted.

POSTURE
  gap              6
  partial          20
  manual           55
  not_applicable   25
  satisfied        19

BY DOMAIN
  Access Control and Authorization           8 controls    57.1%
  Data Management and Protection            14 controls    50.0%
  Disaster Recovery                          7 controls     7.1%
  Email Security                             3 controls      n/a
  Endpoint Security                          4 controls      n/a
  Infrastructure Security                   20 controls    45.5%
  Monitoring and Incident Response          11 controls    45.0%
  Organizational Security                   41 controls    20.3%
  Risk Management                           11 controls     9.1%
  Vulnerability Management                   6 controls     0.0%

CONTROLS (worst first)

  [GAP] CTL-ACC-006  MFA required for infrastructure access
      owner  : shared
      finding: The application performs no multi-factor authentication of its own.
        - Stated plainly rather than deferred: the demo identity model is a bearer username, which is single-factor at best.
        - Remediation: front the API with the agency's identity provider and require MFA there.

  [GAP] CTL-INF-018  Unique production database authentication enforced
      owner  : platform
      finding: The database is using the shipped development password.
        - Reported as a gap rather than hidden: this is exactly the finding a compliance report exists to surface.
        - Override POSTGRES_PASSWORD and NEO4J_PASSWORD before any real deployment.

  [GAP] CTL-ORG-037  Software development lifecycle established
      owner  : platform
      finding: No automated test suite found.

  [GAP] CTL-RSK-008  Software supply chain risks monitored
      owner  : platform
      finding: No dependency manifest or lockfile found.

  [GAP] CTL-VLN-003  Penetration testing performed within the last 12 months
      owner  : shared
      finding: No penetration test has been performed against this application.
        - Required before any deployment handling real evidence.

  [GAP] CTL-VLN-004  Vulnerabilities scanned
      owner  : shared
      finding: No automated vulnerability scanning runs against this codebase or its images.
        - Recorded as a gap rather than omitted. Remediation is routine: dependency audit plus image scanning in CI.

  [PARTIAL] CTL-ACC-004  Employee access regularly reviewed
      owner  : shared
      finding: The platform records access reviews when they are run, but none has been logged yet.
        - Log one with audit action 'access.review' to evidence this control.
        - The mechanism exists; the periodic operation is the agency's.

  [PARTIAL] CTL-ACC-005  Key inventory maintained
      owner  : platform
      finding: Every credential in use is inventoried, but the API bearer token is the username itself — deliberately minimal, and not deployable as-is.
        - app_user rows are the full inventory of API identities.
        - Service credentials: the Postgres DSN and Neo4j auth, both from environment.
        - GAP BY DESIGN: the token carries no secret. Production must terminate on the agency's SSO/PKI; tracex_api.auth.get_principal is shaped as the single seam that changes, so routers stay untouched.

  [PARTIAL] CTL-DAT-002  Data deletion enforced
      owner  : shared
      finding: Case workspace data is deletable; ingested evidence deliberately is not.
        - Cases cascade-delete their pinned entities and notes.
        - ingested_record is append-only on purpose: a hash chain that permits silent deletion is not tamper-evident. Removing a row breaks the chain, and /integrity/verify reports exactly where.
        - TENSION, STATED: retention-driven erasure therefore means disposing of a whole batch and recording the disposal, not editing rows. That procedure is the agency's to write.

  [PARTIAL] CTL-DAT-004  Data encrypted in-transit
      owner  : shared
      finding: No plaintext non-local origin is configured, but the app serves HTTP and relies on a TLS terminator in front of it.
        - CORS origins: https://tracex-web.onrender.com, http://localhost:3000, http://127.0.0.1:3000
        - Inter-service traffic runs on a private container network.

  [PARTIAL] CTL-DAT-012  Key management process implemented
      owner  : shared
      finding: Hashing needs no keys; the service credentials that do exist come from environment configuration with no rotation mechanism.
        - SHA-256 chaining is keyless, so there is no signing key to steal — the trade-off is that the chain proves integrity, not origin.
        - Postgres and Neo4j credentials are injected from environment.
        - GAP: development defaults ship in config. A real deployment must override every one and rotate on a schedule.

  [PARTIAL] CTL-DR-004  Data recovery process established
      owner  : shared
      finding: The recovery path is short and documented: restore Postgres, then rebuild the graph from it.
        - Neo4j is fully derivable from Postgres, so it never needs its own restore.
        - Writing and owning the runbook step is the agency's.

  [PARTIAL] CTL-INF-012  Infrastructure deployed using an infrastructure-as-code tool
      owner  : platform
      finding: No infrastructure-as-code definition found at the repository root.

  [PARTIAL] CTL-INF-013  Key management policy established
      owner  : shared
      finding: Hashing needs no keys; the service credentials that do exist come from environment configuration with no rotation mechanism.
        - SHA-256 chaining is keyless, so there is no signing key to steal — the trade-off is that the chain proves integrity, not origin.
        - Postgres and Neo4j credentials are injected from environment.
        - GAP: development defaults ship in config. A real deployment must override every one and rotate on a schedule.

  [PARTIAL] CTL-INF-015  Production and test environments separated
      owner  : platform
      finding: Running in demo mode: the tamper drill is enabled, so this instance must be treated as non-production.
        - TRACEX_DEMO_MODE=true permits /integrity/drill to mutate a stored record. Correct for a demonstration, unacceptable for an instance holding real evidence.
        - Set TRACEX_DEMO_MODE=false in production; the drill then refuses.
        - seed_on_boot=True

  [PARTIAL] CTL-INF-020  Web Application Firewall (WAF) used
      owner  : shared
      finding: No WAF is deployed in front of the application; the injection class a WAF usually catches is closed at the source instead.
        - Every Cypher query is parameterised and covered by a contract test.
        - Relational access goes through the ORM.
        - A WAF remains advisable at the perimeter and is the agency's to add.

  [PARTIAL] CTL-MON-007  Infrastructure performance monitored
      owner  : shared
      finding: Liveness of every backing service is exposed at /health; there is no metrics history or alerting.
        - Postgres, Neo4j and the LLM provider are each probed.
        - The UI degrades honestly when one is down rather than showing a blank panel that reads as 'no findings'.

  [PARTIAL] CTL-MON-008  Log management used
      owner  : shared
      finding: Application audit events are centralised in Postgres; container and system logs are not aggregated.
        - The security-relevant stream — who did what to which record — is the one that is centralised, indexed and queryable.

  [PARTIAL] CTL-MON-011  Threat intelligence established
      owner  : platform
      finding: The watchlist and campaign-signature mechanisms exist but hold no entries yet.
        - A target is a marker, never a score: an investigator's attention is deliberately excluded from the model's features, so the system cannot simply confirm whatever it was pointed at.

      owner  : shared
      finding: This report is a continuous internal audit of the application's own controls; it is not a substitute for an independent one.
        - Self-assessment by the party being assessed is a starting point, not an assurance opinion. Stated so it is not mistaken for one.

  [PARTIAL] CTL-ORG-021  Offboarding process established
      owner  : shared
      finding: Removing an app_user row revokes all access immediately, because identity is resolved against that table on every request.
        - No session or token survives the removal — there is nothing to expire.
        - Triggering offboarding on a leaver is the agency's process.

  [PARTIAL] CTL-ORG-022  Onboarding process established
      owner  : shared

  [PARTIAL] CTL-RSK-002  Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) completed
      owner  : shared
      finding: No formal DPIA is on file, but the design decisions a DPIA would interrogate are documented and defensible.
        - Data minimisation: only the fields each analysis needs are projected into the graph.
        - Explainability: every risk score ships its own attribution, so an adverse inference can be contested.
        - Exculpatory surfacing: the report generator carries evidence that cuts against the hypothesis, not only for it.
        - A signed DPIA remains the agency's to complete.

  [MANUAL] CTL-DAT-003  Data encrypted at rest
      owner  : agency
      finding: Encryption at rest is a property of the volumes this runs on, which the application cannot observe.
        - Postgres and Neo4j both persist to host-managed volumes.
        - The application adds integrity (SHA-256 chaining), which is a different property from confidentiality and not a substitute for it.
        - Attest with the storage layer's encryption configuration.
